column3: Read, send, and organize HEY email, contacts, and calendars from your terminal.
## Non-negotiable rules
Filter JSON with a built-in jq expression
Output JSON with metadata
Never pipe to an external `jq`; `--jq` is built in and implies `--json`.
it uses stored credentials and refreshes expiring OAuth tokens automatically
If it returns an auth error, follow the retry in [Authentication](#authentication) before you report the task as blocked.
It reports stored credentials without contacting HEY and changes nothing
Use hey auth status --json only when an explicit check is needed.
Never run `hey auth login` unattended; use it only for interactive recovery with the user present.
Write the original HTML to a pipe or file (thread read, journal read, and a contact's note via contact show or contact note show)
`--html` writes the original HTML of `hey thread read`, `hey journal read` and a contact's private note to a pipe or file; a terminal is refused.
Linked accounts share the current login. Use list to discover IDs and use <id|all> to persist the default mail filter; --account overrides it for one invocation.
Never run `hey config trust-local` without the user's explicit approval.
`--jq` filters the full JSON success envelope, so result data is under `.data`.
String results print as plain text; objects and arrays print as formatted JSON.
Use `--quiet --jq` when the expression should run against result data directly.
Errors keep their complete structured envelope.
Commands with raw output of their own (`auth token`, `shell-completion generate`, `setup`, `skill`, `tui`, `--version`, and `timetrack export` without `--output`) reject `--jq`.
Piped or with --json, writes one JSON object per change to stdout (NDJSON), not the usual envelope, and does not apply --jq.

An empty result is an empty array rather than `null`, so `.data[]` is safe on a listing that found nothing.

Output only the count of results

Both answer for what was read, which is the first page unless `--all` or `--limit` reads more, and not every listing warns that more pages exist; `hey screener list --count` is the exception and counts the whole queue.

They work on listings: every `list` command, the thread listings, `hey workflow view`, `hey search`, `hey screener history`, `hey event day|week`, `hey timetrack categories`, `hey attachment list` and `hey thread read` (its entries, read from the index without bodies).
On thread listings they count the postings, not the box, label or contact around them.
